title: Toeplitz circulant and displacement structured solvers

items.title: Toeplitz, circulant, and finite-index conventions for structured solvers
items.statement: Fix zero-based Toeplitz and circulant entries, canonical DFT normalization, coordinate basis vectors, reversal, Hermitian positive-definite convention, lower triangular Toeplitz matrices, and the lag indexing used by this pair.

references.title: Ralf Hiptmair, Numerical Methods for Computational Science and Engineering, Lecture Document, §§4.2.1 and 4.5.1
Daniel Kressner and Robert Luce, Fast computation of the matrix exponential for a Toeplitz matrix, §2

items.title: A specified realified dense residual check bounds the exact residual
items.statement: When the residual is recomputed by the stated real dot-product-and-subtraction DAG, a real system has a gamma_{n+1} componentwise residual enclosure and a complex system has the corresponding gamma_{2n+1} enclosure after explicit realification; no native complex-operation stability claim follows.

references.title: David Bindel, CS 6210: Matrix Computations, Sums, Dots, and Error in Linear Systems

items.title: The canonical finite DFT diagonalizes every circulant
items.statement: A circulant matrix generated by c is diagonalized by the canonical unitary DFT with eigenvalues equal to the unnormalised DFT of c; invertibility and zero-mode compatibility follow exactly.

references.title: Ralf Hiptmair, Numerical Methods for Computational Science and Engineering, Lecture Document, §4.2.1.6–4.2.1.14

items.title: A zero-padded circulant embedding computes a Toeplitz product in O(N log N)
items.statement: For every m-by-n Toeplitz matrix and right-hand side, an explicitly indexed circulant embedding of power-of-two length N at least m+n-1 returns the exact product in exact arithmetic and uses O(N log N) arithmetic operations; finite-precision execution is only conditionally bounded.

references.title: Ralf Hiptmair, Numerical Methods for Computational Science and Engineering, Lecture Document, §4.5.2
Daniel Kressner and Robert Luce, Fast computation of the matrix exponential for a Toeplitz matrix, §1

items.title: Complex Hermitian Toeplitz bordering yields reflection coefficients and positive pivots
items.statement: For the zero-based Hermitian positive-definite Toeplitz leading blocks, the conjugate-reversal bordering recursion solves each lag system, has strictly positive Schur pivots, and requires O(n^2) work and O(n) storage.

references.title: MIT OpenCourseWare 6.341, Discrete-Time Signal Processing, Lecture 13: The Levinson-Durbin Recursion
Ralf Hiptmair, Numerical Methods for Computational Science and Engineering, Lecture Document, §4.5.3

items.title: Lower-shift displacement rank and generator pairs
items.statement: For the fixed lower shift Z, define the Stein displacement A-ZAZ*, its rank, and a generator pair (G,H) satisfying A-ZAZ*=GH*; record the width-r representation as data, not a conditioning claim.

references.title: Daniel Kressner and Robert Luce, Fast computation of the matrix exponential for a Toeplitz matrix, §2.1

items.title: General-RHS Hermitian Toeplitz solve by reflection recursion and Gohberg–Semencul
items.statement: Given a Hermitian Toeplitz input and arbitrary right-hand side, check each reflection pivot, construct the first and last inverse columns, and apply the Gohberg–Semencul triangular-Toeplitz formula without forming dense triangular factors.

references.title: George Labahn and Tamir Shalom, Inversion of Toeplitz Matrices with Only Two Standard Equations, Theorem 1.1
Ralf Hiptmair, Numerical Methods for Computational Science and Engineering, Lecture Document, §4.5.3

items.title: A Toeplitz matrix has lower-shift displacement rank at most two
items.statement: For the fixed lower shift Z, every square Toeplitz matrix T has an explicit two-column generator for T-ZTZ*.

references.title: Daniel Kressner and Robert Luce, Fast computation of the matrix exponential for a Toeplitz matrix, §2.1
Ralf Hiptmair, Numerical Methods for Computational Science and Engineering, Lecture Document, §4.5.1

items.title: One exact scalar elimination step updates a displacement generator
items.statement: If A has a width-s lower-shift displacement generator and its leading scalar pivot d is nonzero, the scalar Schur complement has an explicit width-s generator; exact rank can decrease but cannot exceed s.

references.title: Daniel Kressner and Robert Luce, Fast computation of the matrix exponential for a Toeplitz matrix, Lemma 3.1

items.title: The Hermitian positive-definite Gohberg–Semencul formula is exact and quadratic
items.statement: The first and last inverse columns generated by the complex reflection recursion satisfy the Gohberg–Semencul identity; its application returns T^{-1}b using O(n^2) arithmetic operations and O(n) working storage.

references.title: George Labahn and Tamir Shalom, Inversion of Toeplitz Matrices with Only Two Standard Equations, Theorem 1.1
Daniel Kressner and Robert Luce, Fast computation of the matrix exponential for a Toeplitz matrix, §§2–3.1

title: Toeplitz circulant and displacement structured solvers — Examples

items.title: The periodic Poisson circulant has one compatible zero mode
items.statement: For every N at least 3, the periodic cycle-Laplacian circulant has symbol 2−ω^k−ω^(−k), with only the constant mode zero; compatibility is exactly zero mean. At N=4, the alternating forcing has zero-mean solution f/4.

references.title: Ralf Hiptmair, Numerical Methods for Computational Science and Engineering, Lecture Document, §§4.2.1 and 4.5.1

items.title: An invertible indefinite Toeplitz matrix triggers the pivot-failure branch
items.statement: The matrix [[1,2],[2,1]] is nonsingular but not positive definite, and the Hermitian Toeplitz reflection solver reports its negative second Schur pivot rather than silently claiming an HPD solve.

references.title: Ralf Hiptmair, Numerical Methods for Computational Science and Engineering, Lecture Document, §4.5.3
MIT OpenCourseWare 6.341, Discrete-Time Signal Processing, Lecture 13: The Levinson-Durbin Recursion

items.title: An AR(1) covariance forecast and general-RHS Toeplitz solve
items.statement: For the causal stationary AR(1) covariance with parameter 1/2 and innovation variance 3/4, the two-lag Durbin–Levinson predictor and a separate general right-hand-side Hermitian Toeplitz solve are computed exactly.

references.title: Ralf Hiptmair, Numerical Methods for Computational Science and Engineering, Lecture Document, §4.5.3
MIT OpenCourseWare 6.341, Discrete-Time Signal Processing, Lecture 13: The Levinson-Durbin Recursion
